teams.synopsis: Still #1 despite the first loss of the season — AJ Brown and CMC remain unstoppable.
teams.blurb: Ethan, very controversially, took his first loss this week to a very win-needing team led by Deniz. But he still possesses the best record in the league, and that's earned him the #1 spot in the rankings. <mark class="hl-player">AJ Brown</mark> looks like a monster, and <mark class="hl-player">Mike Evans</mark> has turned back the clock to look like he did in 2017. <mark class="hl-player">Christian McCaffrey</mark> is the definition of unstoppable and has the potential to put up 40+ any time he steps on the field — electric. On top of that, he's getting ready to play a team that hasn't scored over 80 since week 1. Free win.

teams.synopsis: Tied for second, the highest projection in the league — San Giacomos Frannys Fanny is here to stay.
teams.blurb: Speaking of Gorm-sized things, Gorman is in a spot nobody ever expected him to be. He's now tied for second with half the league and boasts the highest projected score this week by a respectable margin. Gorman looks to have had the perfect draft day — he sniffed out diamonds in the rough like Kyren and trusted the classic saying 'the proof is in the pudding' when he went for the veteran back Kamara. Tyreek has been dominant week to week, and Deebo looks like he came to play this year. The only place this team could look to upgrade is tight end, but besides that, San Giacomos Frannys Fanny is here to stay.

teams.synopsis: The league's best RB trio, plus a Gorm-sized target bump for Hockenson with Jefferson out.
teams.blurb: Carmine has the best running back trio in the league — <mark class="hl-player">Pollard</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Swift</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Saquon</mark> all have potential to finish as top-10 running backs, and <mark class="hl-player">TJ Hockenson</mark> is looking primed for a Gorm-sized increase in targets with Justin Jefferson going down. However, his receivers are weak; <mark class="hl-player">Gabe Davis</mark> has been hot recently, but he's not a consistent enough player to be a WR2. Same goes for <mark class="hl-player">Garrett Wilson</mark>, though he's much more talented — it's his QB that isn't. <mark class="hl-player">Zach Wilson</mark> is the only thing holding Garrett back from being the best WR in the league. Carmine only falls in the rankings because he lost this week; his team is as deadly as ever.

teams.synopsis: Diggs and Chase look unstoppable — the running backs remain the shackles on this team's ceiling.
teams.blurb: It physically hurts me to rank Bran this high because I'm not his biggest fan, but his team is performing. Diggs and Chase look like an unstoppable duo as Burrow begins to get back into the swing of things. He does have to hope Kittle can put up 3 touchdowns against the Cowboys and wear an anti-Cowboys shirt every week. His running backs are both pretty weak, but they do have upside and could potentially become a dangerous duo. But today, they remain the shackles on Brandon's playoff aspirations. He's coming up against a struggling Rolls with Butter, so hopefully Bran can continue his success with a dominant win.

teams.synopsis: A controversial 3-2 record aside — David Montgomery has quietly become the real steal of the draft.
teams.blurb: Deniz increased his record to 3-2 this week after a controversial gimme win from Ethan. There have been rumors about whether the respected League Reporter colluded with the website co-manager to hand him a free win — I've heard people saying that. However, it does seem that Deniz has found the real Jahmyr Gibbs of the draft in <mark class="hl-player">David Montgomery</mark>. He's been a beast, to say the least. <mark class="hl-player">Davante Adams</mark> has been his usual stud self, but Deniz just has to hope <mark class="hl-player">Amari Cooper</mark> continues to be good and doesn't become a dud. The future is bright for this young team; Deniz better pray the injury bug leaves Davante alone, or he could be in trouble.

teams.synopsis: A three-week win streak has this team completely turned around — Fields and the WR trio are playing at another level.
teams.blurb: Baylen may have found door number four — Bay has completely turned his season around, going on a 3-week win streak while putting up numbers. <mark class="hl-player">Justin Fields</mark> looks like everything TikTok thought he'd be, and <mark class="hl-player">Zack Moss</mark> doesn't care one bit about <mark class="hl-player">Jonathan Taylor</mark> getting paid. <mark class="hl-player">Pacheco</mark> is the hardest runner in the NFL. The wide receiver trio of <mark class="hl-player">Brown</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Thielen</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Meyers</mark> have all been playing insanely well, and Bay can only hope their production continues — because if it does, be scared. And with <mark class="hl-player">Keaton Mitchell</mark> slated to return soon, Bay should start planning for the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: The Creator finds himself near the bottom of the 3-2 pack — the Jefferson loss is a real blow.
teams.blurb: The Creator is on the lower end of the rest of the 3-2 teams, and this can be attributed to the loss of Justin Jefferson, who was put on IR. While his running backs are very good in Breece Hall and Kenneth, Tutu and Palmer can't be your starting wide receivers, especially with Kupp back. While his big three may be enough to put up triple digits each week, it won't be enough to beat a competent team that can score points. Only time will tell where his team is headed, but one should always be on their toes going face to face with a manager of his caliber.

teams.synopsis: A good week, narrowly edged out by Max — the QB and RB2 spots remain the real concern.
teams.blurb: Aidan Quigley's team had another good week; however, he was barely beat out by the firecracker Max. <mark class="hl-player">Etienne</mark> looks to be a top-10 running back, and <mark class="hl-player">Kelce</mark> is returning to Kelce form. A 3-2 team putting up 125+ will be a threat to any team in the league. However, his team still lost last week and won't be able to advance much in this week's rankings. While this team's future looks bright, his QB and RB2 look apocalyptic at best. If he wants to make the playoffs, he has to do something about this — we'll see how Jetty can pull the strings to make it happen.

teams.synopsis: Down his first-round pick but still fighting — Puka Nacua is quietly keeping this team afloat.
teams.blurb: Always have to feel bad for a man who loses his first-round pick, but Root is not going down without a fight. The emergence of <mark class="hl-player">Puka Nacua</mark> has allowed him to remain positive heading into week 6. An underperforming <mark class="hl-player">Josh Jacobs</mark> has also begun to perform, and Root hopes to combine this with <mark class="hl-player">Lamar 'Action' Jackson</mark> to continue winning. A gritty win last week allowed him to advance to 3-2. However, <mark class="hl-player">Miles Sanders</mark> has been brutal, and he'll have to find an upgrade. Never count the man out — he knows how to get into the playoffs. Also, watch out for his cut-throat negotiation tactics, as reports from League Reporter Deniz Bileydi (@LeagueReporterDenizBileydi) suggest he's in the market to move some pieces.

teams.synopsis: Three straight losses have hit the Nicholas Cruz's hard — explosive WR play is masking a shaky backfield.
teams.blurb: Maney's team has been on the slow decline after 2 amazing weeks in Weeks 2 and 3. Three straight losses have plagued the Nicholas Cruz's, and Maney is hoping he can find the remedy this next week. Not many can blame his previous loss too much but the fantasy gods, as byes and injuries crippled his team. The return of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jordan Addison moving up in the depth chart breathes this team new life. Explosive receivers are what Maney hopes to use to cover up his below-average running back situation — a Derrick Henry who isn't seeing his usual touch share and the Giants backup is not what you want to see. Unless we see a vintage Henry appear in week 6, Maney should consider finding a way to fix these problems. Nothing but blue skies ahead of Maney — he's just gotta remember to get on the train.

teams.synopsis: A dominant win, but 40% of it came from one DJ Moore game — not exactly sustainable.
teams.blurb: Max's team comes off a dominant fantasy win, but that also comes from <mark class="hl-player">DJ Moore</mark> scoring 40% of his total points. While that's no reason to discredit his above-average point total, it's just not sustainable. Max is hoping not only for Moore's dominance to continue, but for <mark class="hl-player">CeeDee</mark>'s to return, as he's been very quiet the past few weeks and is looking primed for a breakout game. However, his strong wide receivers don't address his RB2 problem, as <mark class="hl-player">Jahmyr Gibbs</mark> continues to be a fantasy disappointment — he should either look to deal him or hope he has his breakout game. Max's season is far from over, and we shall see how his future looks.

teams.synopsis: The first win of the season, with Pickens and a healthy Kupp making this team dangerous again.
teams.blurb: Ben got his first win of the season in a close match, and he hopes this win will be a sign of success. The emergence of George Pickens and Kupp returning from injury means Ben's team is a force to be reckoned with for the rest of the year. He recently acquired A-a-ron Jones from The Creator, which he hopes will help his poor running back situation. Ben hopes he can scrape by this week without Pickens and Jones and begin his comeback to fantasy relevance. Although if he's to go far, he has to find an answer at QB, because Joshua Dobbs is not the answer.

teams.synopsis: Another loss for the former top-5 staple — Richardson's injury forces Purdy into the lineup.
teams.blurb: Another L for the previous staple of the top 5 spots in the rankings. Not how he expected or hoped for the season to start out. Kelly is hoping a healthy Jonathan Taylor can help his team dig its way out, but after last week, who knows with that backfield. Anthony Richardson's injury is a massive blow, as he's now starting Brock Purdy. While the season is still young, it's looking like Rolls with Butter will not be making the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: Time is running out — win now or the season's effectively over.
teams.blurb: I'm done talking about this team. Win now or the season is over. Last thing I'll say: never pick a fight with a man who has nothing left to lose.
